notes: Parts are unchanged from step 1: Leonardo, breadboard, pushbutton, and two jumper wires (blue and black).
No resistor is used: the sketch enables INPUT_PULLUP on pin 2, so the pin reads high until the button connects it to GND.

Wiring follows the circuit image. The blue wire goes from pin 2 to column 6, row i, which is the strip of the button's right-hand legs. The black wire goes from the GND pin next to 5V to column 4, row c, which is the strip of the button's left-hand legs. Pressing the button joins pin 2 to GND.

Breadboard hole names follow the catalogue convention: bank 'b' holds rows f-j and bank 't' holds rows a-e. The image prints the labels with j-f in the top half and e-a in the bottom half. The button straddles the centre gap in columns 4 and 6, with its top legs in row f and its bottom legs in row e.
In the button's port naming, side 1 is the left pair (column 4) and side 2 is the right pair (column 6). The two pins of each pair are joined inside the button.
The GND header pin used is assumed to be GND.1. The image highlights the upper of the two GND pins beside 5V.
